items.title: Spend less time on operational busywork and resolve incidents faster with Grafana Workflows
items.summary: You're investigating checkout errors when someone asks who's coordinating the incident. Support needs an update, and another responder is looking for the runbook. You stop what you're doing to get everyone pointed in the same direction.They're all reasonable requests, but each one takes your attention away from understanding the problem. Yes, your team has a process for handling incidents, but carrying it out is another job for someone who's already busy.Grafana Workflows, available in public preview, turns your team’s processes into automated steps across Grafana Cloud and your other tools. You can even include Grafana Assistant in those steps to investigate an issue, summarize findings, or draft an update. For example, a workflow can create an incident channel, page support according to your team’s rules, and ask Assistant to prepare a briefing from the available evidence.The same approach works with your typical day-to-day operations. Once you define the workflow, Grafana Cloud can prepare the next engineer's handoff or gather the findings for your weekly service review. You decide what should happen consistently and where AI can help make sense of changing information.Get the incident response movingTo illustrate how your team can benefit from Workflows, let's walk through a major incident response process.For starters, your team needs a place to collaborate and someone to coordinate the response. A runbook helps, but someone still has to find the on-call commander, open the channel, and share the right links.Workflows include blueprints, prebuilt templates you can adapt to your team's process. For this type of project, you'd start with the major incident kickoff blueprint, which can automatically respond to an active critical incident in Grafana Cloud IRM, including an incident that has just been escalated to critical.It creates a linked Slack channel, looks up your incident commander schedule, and assigns an on-call commander. It also posts your response instructions, bookmarks the runbook and incident page, and records the kickoff on the timeline. If nobody is on call, it leaves a note so the team knows to assign a commander.Now responders have the incident record and runbook at hand, and the commander can start coordinating the investigation. The setup follows the process you've configured. From there, you can build on that foundation. Suppose your policy is to involve support in every critical incident. Simply add a step that pages your support team in IRM and another that shares the incident link in their Slack channel. Support can get involved while engineers investigate, without waiting for someone to remember another handoff.Note: Workflows is currently available under "More apps" in your Grafana Cloud navigation menu.Put AI findings where people need themGetting everyone together is just the beginning. The next person to join will need to know what's happening, what you've checked, and where to look next.Extend the kickoff workflow with an ask Assistant step. Give Workflows the incident link, the affected service, and a specific task:Review this incident and the available error and latency signals around its start time. Summarize the observed symptoms, link to the evidence, and suggest the next checks. Separate observations from hypotheses and flag missing information.Assistant investigates using the available observability context and returns a briefing. Subsequent workflow steps post the briefing to the incident channel and add it to the incident timeline. The team can follow the evidence and ask better questions, and those who join later have a starting point for catching up.At the same time, support has a different need. They have to turn technical findings into clear, customer-facing updates. An incident status update could trigger a workflow that asks Assistant to draft that explanation from the confirmed facts. A post message to Slack channel step sends the draft to the internal support channel, where the team reviews and edits it before sharing it externally.This is where combining rules and AI becomes useful. You define the trigger, the task, and the destination. Assistant interprets the supplied context and returns a result that the next step can use. An engineer doesn't have to copy the answer out of a chat and put it in the right place.You can also use AI to answer a specific question that determines the next step in your response. For example, when an alert fires, a workflow could ask Assistant to assess whether customers are affected and estimate how many. If the result exceeds a threshold you define, the workflow can declare an incident and page the SRE on-call. This focused assessment can run alongside a broader investigation into the root cause.Give the next on-call engineer a head startSoon after, the rotation changes, and the incoming engineer asks, "Anything I should know?"Answering that question sufficiently can take some work.
